purpose: Freeze neutral fixture values so the comparison isolates transition mechanism rather than speed, easing, amplitude, or layout differences.

CS1_SYNCHRONIZED_SETTLE.outgoing: no animated choreography; removed before incoming treatment begins
CS1_SYNCHRONIZED_SETTLE.incoming: one field-level translateY from negative context amplitude to 0

CS3_OPPOSED_FIELD_EXCHANGE.outgoing: one field-level translateY from 0 to positive context amplitude
CS3_OPPOSED_FIELD_EXCHANGE.incoming: one field-level translateY from negative context amplitude to 0

layout.field_geometry: Outgoing and incoming fields occupy the same fixed content frame. Neutral content density and structure are identical across candidates.
layout.context_adaptation: Only transform amplitude changes between APP and WEB for CS1/CS3. Timing/easing/content/layout remain invariant.

replay.activation: Cancel any existing candidate animations, restore Context A synchronously, then execute exactly one transition to Context B.
replay.interruption: A new replay or authoritative state change cancels stale animation immediately. No queued completion or aesthetic catch-up.

reduced_motion.behavior: Cancel any active transition animation and render Context B synchronously.
reduced_motion.semantic_equivalence: Context B content, function and state are identical to the full-motion final state.

preflight_assertions: 16 unique FULL matrix cells: CS0-CS3 × APP/WEB × WIDE/320.
The same 16 cells pass forced reduced motion.
No field contains element-level animation or nonzero delay.
CS1 creates exactly one incoming field animation and no outgoing animation.
CS2 creates exactly two simultaneous field opacity animations.
CS3 creates exactly two simultaneous field transform animations.
Animated candidates use exactly 280 ms and cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1).
CS1/CS3 translation amplitude is exactly 16px APP and 32px WEB.
Final Context B state is equivalent under FULL and REDUCED modes.
